question: Which of the following is NOT one of the six basic vehicle control skills test exercises listed in the manual?
choice_a: Three-point turn
choice_b: Straight line backing
choice_c: Offset back/right
choice_d: Alley dock
explanation: The manual lists six exercises: straight line backing, offset back/right, offset back/left, parallel park (driver side), parallel park (conventional), and alley dock. A three-point turn is not among them.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test (exercise list)

question: The manual identifies four categories used to score the basic control skills test. Which of the following is one of them?
choice_a: Speed control
choice_b: Encroachments
choice_c: Signal timing
choice_d: Fuel efficiency
explanation: The four scoring categories are Crossing Boundaries (encroachments), Pull-ups, Outside Vehicle Observations (looks), and Final Position/Inside Parallel.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 12.1 - Scoring

question: According to the manual, what is scored as an "encroachment" during the basic control skills test?
choice_a: Stopping without changing direction
choice_b: Opening the door to check position
choice_c: Touching or crossing over an exercise boundary line or cone with any portion of the vehicle
choice_d: Taking longer than average to complete the exercise
explanation: The examiner scores the number of times you touch or cross over an exercise boundary line or cone with any portion of your vehicle; each is counted as an error.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 12.1 - Scoring (Encroachments)

question: Under the manual's scoring rules, when is a stop-and-forward movement scored as a "pull-up"?
choice_a: Whenever the driver comes to a complete stop
choice_b: Any time the parking brake is applied
choice_c: Whenever the driver checks a mirror
choice_d: When a driver stops and pulls forward to clear an encroachment or to get a better position
explanation: A pull-up is scored when a driver stops and pulls forward to clear an encroachment or to get a better position; stopping without changing direction does not count as a pull-up.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 12.1 - Scoring (Pull-ups)

question: What does the manual say about initial pull-ups during the skills test?
choice_a: You will not be penalized for initial pull-ups
choice_b: Any pull-up results in automatic failure
choice_c: Only bus drivers are permitted pull-ups
choice_d: Pull-ups are only allowed during the alley dock exercise
explanation: The manual states you will not be penalized for initial pull-ups; however, an excessive number of pull-ups will count as errors.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 12.1 - Scoring (Pull-ups)

question: What happens if a driver makes an excessive number of pull-ups during the skills test?
choice_a: Nothing, pull-ups are never scored
choice_b: It will count as errors
choice_c: It automatically fails the driver regardless of other factors
choice_d: It only matters during the parallel park exercises
explanation: The manual states that while initial pull-ups are not penalized, an excessive number of pull-ups will count as errors.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 12.1 - Scoring (Pull-ups)

question: Before exiting the vehicle to check its external position during the skills test, what must the driver do?
choice_a: Turn off the engine completely
choice_b: Sound the horn to alert the examiner
choice_c: Place the vehicle in neutral and set the parking brake(s)
choice_d: Roll down all windows
explanation: When permitted to stop and exit the vehicle to check its position (a "look"), the driver must place the vehicle in neutral and set the parking brake(s) before exiting.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 12.1 - Scoring (Outside Vehicle Observations)

question: When exiting the vehicle to take a "look" during the skills test, how must the driver exit safely?
choice_a: By facing away from the vehicle and walking quickly
choice_b: By jumping down from the cab
choice_c: By exiting only through the passenger-side door
choice_d: By facing the vehicle and maintaining three points of contact with the vehicle at all times
explanation: The manual requires exiting safely by facing the vehicle and maintaining three points of contact with the vehicle at all times.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 12.1 - Scoring (Outside Vehicle Observations)

topic: Exiting a Bus for a Look
question: When exiting a bus to take a "look" during the skills test, what additional requirement applies?
choice_a: The driver must maintain a firm grasp on the handrail at all times
choice_b: The driver must exit through the rear emergency door
choice_c: The driver must have a passenger hold the door
choice_d: The driver must remove their seatbelt before the bus stops moving
explanation: When exiting a bus, the driver must maintain a firm grasp on the handrail at all times, in addition to the general three-points-of-contact requirement.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 12.1 - Scoring (Outside Vehicle Observations)

question: What can result in an automatic failure of the basic control skills test?
choice_a: Taking more than five minutes to complete an exercise
choice_b: Failing to safely secure the vehicle or safely exit it when taking a "look"
choice_c: Asking the examiner a question
choice_d: Using a manual transmission vehicle
explanation: If you do not safely secure the vehicle or safely exit it, it may result in an automatic failure of the basic control skills test.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 12.1 - Scoring (Outside Vehicle Observations)

question: What is the maximum number of times a driver may exit the vehicle to check its position ("look") during most skills test exercises?
choice_a: One
choice_b: Unlimited
choice_c: Two
choice_d: Three
explanation: The maximum number of times you may look to check the position of your vehicle is two, except for the Straight Line Backing exercise, which allows only one look.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 12.1 - Scoring (Outside Vehicle Observations)

question: How many "looks" are permitted during the Straight Line Backing exercise specifically?
choice_a: Zero
choice_b: Two
choice_c: Three
choice_d: One
explanation: The Straight Line Backing exercise allows only one look, unlike other exercises which allow up to two.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 12.1 - Scoring (Outside Vehicle Observations)

question: According to the manual, which of the following counts as a scored "look"?
choice_a: Opening the door or moving from a seated position while in physical control of the vehicle, or on a bus, walking to the back to get a better view
choice_b: Checking a side mirror without stopping
choice_c: Using the turn signal before backing
choice_d: Braking smoothly before a stop
explanation: Each time the driver opens the door, moves from a seated position while in physical control of the vehicle, or (on a bus) walks to the back to get a better view, it is scored as a "look."
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 12.1 - Scoring (Outside Vehicle Observations)

question: What does the manual say about finishing an exercise in its "final position"?
choice_a: It is optional as long as the vehicle is within the boundaries
choice_b: The driver must finish each exercise exactly as the examiner has instructed, or be penalized and could fail
choice_c: Final position only applies to the alley dock exercise
choice_d: Final position is scored the same as an encroachment
explanation: The manual states it is important to finish each exercise exactly as instructed by the examiner; failing to maneuver into the final position as described can result in penalty and possible failure.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 12.1 - Scoring (Final Position/Inside Parallel)

question: What must a driver do during the Straight Line Backing exercise?
choice_a: Parallel park the vehicle on the right side of the road
choice_b: Back the vehicle into an alley within three feet of the rear boundary
choice_c: Back the vehicle in a straight line between two rows of cones without touching or crossing the exercise boundaries
choice_d: Drive forward through a series of cones at posted speed
explanation: In Straight Line Backing, the driver backs the vehicle in a straight line between two rows of cones without touching or crossing over the exercise boundaries.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 12.2.1 - Straight Line Backing

question: In the Offset Back/Right exercise, where must the driver back the vehicle?
choice_a: Into a space to the left rear of the vehicle
choice_b: Into an alley on the sight side
choice_c: Into a parking space on the driver's left
choice_d: Into the opposite lane, to the right rear, until the front of the vehicle passes the first set of cones
explanation: In Offset Back/Right, after driving straight forward past the outer boundary, the driver backs into the opposite lane (to the right rear) until the front of the vehicle has passed the first set of cones, without striking boundary lines or cones.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 12.2.2 - Offset Back/Right

question: The Offset Back/Left exercise requires the driver to back the vehicle into a space located:
choice_a: To the left rear of the vehicle
choice_b: Directly behind the vehicle
choice_c: To the right rear of the vehicle
choice_d: Diagonally in front of the vehicle
explanation: Offset Back/Left requires backing into a space to the left rear of the vehicle, driving straight forward past the outer boundary first, then backing into the opposite lane until the front passes the first set of cones.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 12.2.3 - Offset Back/Left

question: In the Parallel Park (Driver Side) exercise, the parking space is located:
choice_a: On the driver's right
choice_b: On the driver's left
choice_c: Directly behind an alley
choice_d: Diagonally across two lanes
explanation: In Parallel Park (Driver Side), the driver parks in a space on their left, driving past the entrance with the vehicle parallel to the parking area, then backing in without crossing boundaries.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 12.2.4 - Parallel Park (Driver Side)

question: In the Parallel Park (Conventional) exercise, the parking space is located:
choice_a: On the driver's left
choice_b: Behind the vehicle in a straight line
choice_c: On the driver's right
choice_d: In an alley
explanation: In Parallel Park (Conventional), the driver parks in a space on their right, as opposed to the left-side space used in the Driver Side version.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 12.2.5 - Parallel Park (Conventional)

question: For both parallel park exercises, what must the driver accomplish besides avoiding boundary lines and cones?
choice_a: Complete the maneuver in under 60 seconds
choice_b: Use only the driver-side mirror
choice_c: Signal continuously throughout the maneuver
choice_d: Get the entire vehicle completely into the space
explanation: For both parallel park exercises, the driver is required to get the entire vehicle completely into the space, in addition to not crossing the front, side, or rear boundaries marked by cones.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 12.2.4-12.2.5 - Parallel Park Exercises

question: What is required for the Alley Dock exercise?
choice_a: Sight-side back the vehicle into an alley, bringing the rear of the vehicle within three feet of the rear of the alley without touching boundary lines or cones
choice_b: Drive straight through the alley without stopping
choice_c: Back the vehicle into the alley using only mirrors, with no distance requirement
choice_d: Park the vehicle parallel to the curb outside the alley
explanation: In the Alley Dock exercise, the driver sight-side backs into the alley, bringing the rear of the vehicle within three feet of the rear of the alley without touching boundary lines or cones.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 12.2.6 - Alley Dock

question: Upon completing the Alley Dock maneuver, what must be true about the vehicle's position?
choice_a: The vehicle must be facing the opposite direction it started
choice_b: The vehicle must be straight within the alley/lane
choice_c: The vehicle must be touching the rear boundary
choice_d: The vehicle must have made at least one pull-up
explanation: The manual specifies that the vehicle must be straight within the alley/lane when the alley dock maneuver has been completed.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 12.2.6 - Alley Dock

question: According to the manual, where might the basic control skills exercises be tested?
choice_a: Only in a closed off-road course
choice_b: Only during the on-road driving test
choice_c: Off-road or somewhere on the street during the road test
choice_d: Only at the driver's home terminal
explanation: The manual states basic control skills could be tested using one or more of the listed exercises off-road or somewhere on the street during the road test.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 12 - Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test (introduction)

question: If a driver simply stops the vehicle without changing direction during a skills test exercise, how is this scored?
choice_a: As an encroachment
choice_b: As a pull-up
choice_c: As an automatic failure
choice_d: It does not count as a pull-up
explanation: The manual explicitly states that stopping without changing direction does not count as a pull-up.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 12.1 - Scoring (Pull-ups)

question: During the on-road driving test, which of the following is a requirement stated in the manual?
choice_a: Complete the test without an accident or moving violation
choice_b: Reach highway speed within the first mile
choice_c: Use the horn at every intersection
choice_d: Keep the radio off at all times
explanation: The manual requires drivers to wear a safety belt, obey all traffic signs, signals, and laws, and complete the test without an accident or moving violation.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 13.1 - How You Will Be Tested

question: What happens if the test route does not include a certain traffic situation, such as a railroad crossing?
choice_a: The examiner skips that scoring category entirely
choice_b: The driver may be asked to simulate the situation by telling the examiner what they are or would be doing
choice_c: The test is automatically extended to another route
choice_d: The driver fails that category by default
explanation: If the test route does not have certain traffic situations, the driver may be asked to simulate it by telling the examiner what they are or would be doing in that situation.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 13.1 - How You Will Be Tested

question: According to the manual, when does "unsafe coasting" occur?
choice_a: Whenever the vehicle exceeds the speed limit
choice_b: When the driver fails to signal a turn
choice_c: When the vehicle is out of gear (clutch depressed or gearshift in neutral) for more than the length of the vehicle
choice_d: When the parking brake is engaged while moving
explanation: Unsafe coasting occurs when the vehicle is out of gear, with the clutch depressed or gearshift in neutral, for more than the length of the vehicle.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 13.1.1 - Turns

question: If stopping behind another vehicle, where should the driver stop according to the manual?
choice_a: Close enough to read the license plate
choice_b: At least three vehicle lengths back regardless of visibility
choice_c: Wherever traffic allows, distance is not specified
choice_d: Where the driver can see the rear tires on the vehicle ahead (a safe gap)
explanation: The manual instructs that if stopping behind another vehicle, the driver should stop where they can see the rear tires on the vehicle ahead (a safe gap).
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 13.1.1 - Turns

question: While driving through an intersection, what does the manual instruct regarding lane changes?
choice_a: Do not change lanes while proceeding through the intersection
choice_b: Lane changes are encouraged to keep traffic moving
choice_c: Lane changes are only allowed at four-way stops
choice_d: Lane changes must be completed before entering the intersection
explanation: When driving through an intersection, the manual states not to change lanes while proceeding through it.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 13.1.2 - Intersections

question: During the urban business portion of the on-road test, where should the vehicle be positioned?
choice_a: Centered in the left-most lane at all times
choice_b: Centered in the proper lane (right-most lane), keeping up with traffic flow but not exceeding the posted speed limit
choice_c: Straddling two lanes for visibility
choice_d: As close to parked cars as possible
explanation: During urban business driving, the vehicle should be centered in the proper (right-most) lane, keeping up with the flow of traffic without exceeding the posted speed limit.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 13.1.3 - Urban Business

question: What must a driver do before changing lanes during the multiple-lane portion of the test?
choice_a: Signal only after beginning the lane change
choice_b: Accelerate rapidly before signaling
choice_c: Make the necessary traffic checks first, then use proper signals and change lanes smoothly when safe
choice_d: Change lanes only when directed by another vehicle
explanation: For lane changes, the driver should make the necessary traffic checks first, then use proper signals and smoothly change lanes when it is safe to do so.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 13.1.4 - Lane Changes

question: When performing the Stop/Start maneuver (pulling over to check something on the vehicle), what must the driver activate once stopped?
choice_a: High-beam headlights
choice_b: The horn
choice_c: The rear defroster
choice_d: Hazard/four-way emergency flashers
explanation: Once stopped for the Stop/Start maneuver, the driver must cancel the turn signal, activate the four-way emergency flashers, apply the parking brake, and shift to neutral or park.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 13.1.6 - Stop/Start

question: When resuming from the Stop/Start maneuver, what does the manual specifically caution against?
choice_a: Turning the wheel before the vehicle moves
choice_b: Checking traffic before pulling away
choice_c: Releasing the parking brake
choice_d: Activating the left turn signal
explanation: The manual instructs the driver to release the parking brake and pull straight ahead, and specifically not to turn the wheel before the vehicle moves.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 13.1.6 - Stop/Start

question: For a bus, school bus, or vehicle displaying placards, within what distance from the nearest rail must the vehicle stop at a railroad crossing?
choice_a: Within 100 feet but not less than 50 feet
choice_b: Within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet
choice_c: Within 25 feet but not less than 5 feet
choice_d: Exactly 10 feet from the nearest rail
explanation: These vehicles must stop the vehicle within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 13.1.8 - Railroad Crossing

question: What should a driver do before entering a curve, according to the manual?
choice_a: Accelerate to maintain momentum through the curve
choice_b: Shift into neutral to coast through the curve
choice_c: Reduce speed so that further braking or shifting is not required in the curve
choice_d: Change lanes to get the best line through the curve
explanation: Before entering a curve, the driver should reduce speed so that further braking or shifting is not required while in the curve.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 13.1.7 - Curve

question: According to the manual's lane usage rules, where should a vehicle finish a left turn on a multiple-lane road?
choice_a: In the far left (fast) lane
choice_b: In the right-most (curb) lane
choice_c: Straddling the center line
choice_d: In the lane directly to the right of the center line
explanation: The manual states a vehicle should finish a left turn in the lane directly to the right of the center line on a multiple-lane road, while a right turn should finish in the right-most (curb) lane.
source_note: Tennessee CDL Manual, Section 13.1.14(d) - Lane Usage
